trigger: a new record (POST or MCP) with different operator exceptions on a device that is still contained, e.g. after a forced end the device never acted on

summary: Clustered con-1 = UP-2 (two independent reporters in the Gate 4 wave). The device kept its earlier allow set and the server confirmed the new record anyway. Fixed: the device now reports a kept allow set only when operator exceptions differ as a set, and the server leaves a never-confirmed record unconfirmed, writes one allow_set_not_applied failure row and the unconfirmed alert fires. The new whitelist is not applied automatically; the remedy is release, then quarantine again (disclosed). The time-limit half is closed by B8. fixed in f34102027 (gate-fix: governance r1); re-reviewed at e23166a2c

adjudicated_by: architect role of the change pipeline (a reviewer separate from the engineer who wrote the code), confirmed by the project owner at the push gate; separation: de-escalation rule; independence asserted, not verified
adjudication_rationale: Inapplicable as a defect of this change: the device holds one containment state, so a direct apply over a still-contained device changes nothing and the owed release lifts exactly the containment it is owed for; the remaining case needs a containment sent outside the quarantine routes, which the docs state is not recorded, listed, re-applied or protected. Disclosed instead of fixed by owner ruling.
waiver_rationale: Residual accepted by the owner: a containment applied outside the quarantine routes after a forced end can be lifted by the owed release; documented with the remedy (quarantine again through the routes).

Disclosed in security-hardening.md (Forced end) and the reconciler header.

trigger: the server acted on a time limit reported by the device
classification_rationale: a value reported by the device could end a record the server applied
summary: UP-5. Rule now in force (owner ruling): a device-reported time limit never ends a server-applied record. The value is no longer parsed, stored or acted on; an inactive answer on an active record is drift and the containment is re-applied. A record ends only on the device's inactive answer after a release, or an operator's forced end. Routed-concern row clause 5 and the docs say so. fixed in f34102027 (gate-fix: governance r1); re-reviewed at e23166a2c
